summary: The note traces salt block grilling from its Himalayan origins along trade routes to Asia, Europe and the Americas, and describes its resurgence since fall 2023. It covers regional variants such as Japan's Shioyaki and Scandinavian gravlax, the science of heat distribution and the melted salt barrier, practical heating and cleaning tips, and the method's appeal for sustainability and low-sodium diets.
one_line: Salt block grilling, an ancient Himalayan technique, has revived since fall 2023, with its history, global variants, science, methods and modern appeal covered.
key_facts: Salt block grilling has seen a resurgence in popularity since the fall of 2023.
Early records show salt block cooking originated in the Himalayas, where people used natural blocks of rock salt to grill and cure food.
By the time Marco Polo traveled in the late 13th century, salt block cooking had become a culinary touchstone in many parts of Asia.
In September 2023, culinary historian Stefano Garcia lectured at the University of Gastronomy on how the method reached the Americas, where European settlers introduced block grilling.
In Japan the practice is called Shioyaki, where fish is grilled on salt blocks to give a delicate, umami-packed crust.
In Scandinavia, large salt slabs have been used to serve and cure salmon, giving rise to gravlax.
Chef James Miller opened the restaurant "Salt & Stone" in New York City in October 2023, using Himalayan salt blocks.
Dr. Rosalind Chu published research on September 15, 2023, explaining that a small layer of salt melts when the block is heated and forms a barrier that limits how much salt enters the food.
The uniform crystal structure of the block distributes heat evenly, and its low porosity minimizes moisture absorption, creating a dry heat surface.
Chef Elena Martinez of the cooking school "La Cocina del Sal" recommends heating a block slowly over about an hour to prevent cracking.
Thin meats, delicate seafood and vegetables can be seared directly on the block, while thicker cuts may need a pre-cooked sear first.
After use, a cooled block should be scraped and wiped with a damp cloth and never submerged in water; with care it lasts several cooking sessions.
Chef Michaela DeSouza opened the eco-conscious restaurant "Earth Table" in September 2023 and uses salt block cooking as a symbol of purity and environmental responsibility.
The light seasoning from the block suits low-sodium diets and adds trace minerals found in pink Himalayan salt.
